name: Greater Yellowstone
blurb: Wolves, elk, willow and beaver on North America's northern range.
story: Yellowstone anchors one of the last large, nearly intact ecosystems of the northern temperate zone: about 22 million acres of the central Rockies. Elk, bison and moose feed the wolves and grizzlies. Grizzlies also rely on whitebark pine seeds, and an introduced rust disease is killing the trees.
matters: It is a natural laboratory in landscape ecology, and everything in it is linked. Aspen have declined 50 to 95% on the northern range since 1872, and osprey around Yellowstone Lake have declined with the cutthroat trout.

tip.title: Try the gray wolf
tip.text: Wolves were reintroduced in 1995. Many ecologists link their return to less elk browsing on willow and aspen, and to more beaver habitat. Open the wolf, then use the what-if slider.

nodes.desc: Clonal groves that shelter birds and insects. Elk and beaver browse young shoots, which can stop a grove from regrowing.
Evergreen winter forage. Pronghorn lean on it when snow buries the grass.
A high-elevation pine whose fatty seeds feed grizzly bears and red squirrels.
Nymphs graze algae on stream stones and are a main food for cutthroat trout.
Cuts willow and aspen and dams streams. The ponds it makes are used by fish, birds and moose.
Wades into streamside willow thickets, its main winter food.
The northern range's main large grazer and browser. Wolves, cougars, coyotes and bears all take elk.

nodes.name: Bison
nodes.desc: Grazes grass and sedge in large herds. Winter-killed animals feed scavengers.
Browses sagebrush, willow and grass at lower elevations.
Open-country grazer and sagebrush browser. Coyotes and eagles take fawns.
Chew grasses all summer, then feed songbirds, and trout when they fall into streams.
A small grass-eating rodent and a staple for foxes, coyotes, hawks and eagles.

nodes.name: Ground squirrel
nodes.desc: A hibernating meadow rodent eaten by nearly every mid-sized predator. Grizzlies dig them out of burrows.

nodes.name: Red squirrel
nodes.desc: Stores whitebark pine cones in middens, which grizzly bears raid.

nodes.name: River otter
nodes.desc: Hunts trout and other fish along streams and lake shores.
Dives for trout from perches over rivers and lakes.
Takes fish and scavenges carcasses, including wolf kills.
Ravens often follow wolves and feed on what they leave behind.
Hunts voles and ground squirrels, takes fawns and calves, and scavenges wolf kills. Wolves also kill coyotes.
Pounces on voles beneath the snow and takes ground squirrels.
A grassland songbird that eats grasshoppers and seeds in summer.
Hunts voles, ground squirrels and meadow birds from open perches.
Hunts ground squirrels and voles, takes pronghorn fawns, and scavenges kills.
Reintroduced in 1995. Hunts elk, bison, deer and moose, and its kills feed scavengers. Many ecologists link its return to recovering willow and aspen.
An omnivore that eats pine seeds, roots, trout, elk calves and carrion.

nodes.name: Mountain lion
nodes.desc: An ambush hunter of elk and mule deer in broken, wooded terrain.
Powers photosynthesis. Nearly all the energy in this web starts here.
Holds the nitrogen and minerals that plants draw up. Decomposers return nutrients from litter and carcasses.

nodes.name: Fungi & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down plant litter and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
